transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
The attorney general of New York is leading a criminal investigation into an alleged gang
rape at Cornell University.
As NPR's Brian Mann reports, New York Democratic Governor Kathy Hochul appointed A.G. Letitia
James saying she wants answers about why the 2024 case was not fully investigated.
Hochul says she's troubled by the behavior of university leaders, campus police, and
a local prosecutor who dropped the investigation two years ago after seeing only a partial
transcript of the woman's allegations.
"I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug."
Letitia James, the state attorney general, will now take over the criminal probe.
Hochul says she'll also push to close a loophole in state law that makes it harder to prosecute
sex crimes when the victim has been drinking or using drugs.
"Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape, period."
Cornell University has also agreed to Hochul's demand that an outside counsel review the
school's handling of the case.
Brian Mann, NPR News, Ithaca, New York.
A new report from the Labor Department shows hiring slowed last month.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs in September while
the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2 percent.
Hiring in September was weaker than forecasters had expected and job gains for July and August
were revised downward.
Restaurants and retailers continue to add jobs in September, but at a lackluster pace.
Financial services and government both cut jobs during the month.
The unemployment rate rose slightly in September as several hundred thousand people joined
the workforce, but the jobless rate is still low by historical standards.
Average wages were up three percent from a year ago, that's a smaller annual gain than
the previous month, and probably not enough to keep pace with rising prices.
Workers buying power has been eroding for much of the year as inflation has outpaced
pay increases.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics says more than 7 million people are unemployed in the U.S.
While the unemployment rate among U.S. workers is around 4.2 percent, it is sharply higher
among black people, increasing in September to 7 percent.
Under pressure from President Trump, G7 countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels
of diesel and crude oil.
Here's French President Emmanuel Macron today announcing the decision to release strategic
reserves over the next four months, starting with diesel.
Much of the globe's delivery network depends on the fuel, which has climbed a record highs
in the United States and to the forefront of voter worries a month before the midterm
elections.
After nine years as NFL game analyst for CBS Sports, Tony Romo's tenure has formally
ended.
The network confirmed his departure more than a month after the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback
pleaded no contest to the charge of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
Attorneys for a Tennessee death row inmate say in a court filing today that their client
was placed on a ventilator and unconscious in a hospital in the hours following her failed
execution Wednesday.
They say hospital staff worked to save Christa Pike's life and clear the two doses of a lethal
drug pentobarbital that the state uses in its executions.
The botched process prompted Governor Bill Lee to halt further executions in the state,
pending a third party review.
Iowa lawmakers are in a one-day special session to consider tax incentives for a new steel
plant President Trump announced this week.
Iowa Public Radio's Grant Gerlach has more.
Minnesota-based Misabi Metallic says its proposed $15 billion facility in southeast Iowa could
employ more than 1,700 people.
Iowa's Republican-led legislature is considering state tax credits worth up to 10 percent on
that investment over 10 years.
Democratic State Senator Janice Weiner questions why they're rushing to revise state incentives
less than a week after the project was announced.
It doesn't clean up our water.
It doesn't address our cancer epidemic.
It doesn't make child care easier to find or afford.
Residents are touting the project as an historic investment.
It could be a boost for GOP candidates in tight races in Iowa for the U.S. House and
Senate and for Governor.
For NPR News, I'm Grant Gerlach in Des Moines.
Amazon is pledging a billion-dollar investment in data center communities as the facility's
heavy reliance on electricity and water face public pushback this midterm election year.
Executive Matt Garman also says in a blog post today Amazon is no longer using non-disclosure
agreements with government partners on projects.
